name: César Pelli
blurb: Designed elegant supertall towers, including the twin Petronas Towers, favoring refined skins over a signature style across global skylines.

name: Glenn Murcutt
blurb: Pritzker laureate working solo, designing lightweight, climate-tuned houses that "touch the earth lightly."

name: Adolf Loos
blurb: Provocateur who branded ornament a crime, championing smooth facades and spatial 'Raumplan' interiors of interlocking split levels.

name: Hans Hollein
blurb: Austrian postmodernist who blended art, commerce and sculptural monumentality in richly detailed museums and glittering boutique shopfronts.

name: Otto Wagner
blurb: Vienna Secession pioneer who shed historicist ornament for functional, boldly modern civic buildings clad in marble and aluminium bolts.

name: Marina Tabassum
blurb: Crafts a spiritual, climate-rooted modernism in brick and light, from luminous mosques to flood-resilient homes for the poor.

name: Victor Horta
blurb: Belgian Art Nouveau originator who dissolved walls into whiplash iron tendrils, glass and daylight within flowing bourgeois townhouses.

name: Lina Bo Bardi
blurb: Fused bold concrete-and-glass modernism with Brazilian popular culture, craft and generous public space.

name: Oscar Niemeyer
blurb: Sculpted sweeping reinforced-concrete curves that defined the modernist capital of Brasília.

name: Paulo Mendes da Rocha
blurb: Leading figure of Paulista Brutalism, celebrated for bold, spare concrete structures and civic public space.

name: Diébédo Francis Kéré
blurb: Pritzker laureate raising climate-smart schools and civic halls from local clay, community hands and passively cooled, daylight-flooded overhanging roofs.

name: Frank Gehry
blurb: Deconstructivist known for sculptural, titanium-clad curves that turned buildings into billowing metallic forms.
credit: City of Toronto / Jose San Juan

name: Moshe Safdie
blurb: Humanises megastructures through modular Habitat housing and light-filled, garden-woven civic complexes.

name: Alejandro Aravena
blurb: Champions socially engaged "incremental" housing and civic architecture, giving low-income residents half a good house they can expand themselves.

name: I. M. Pei
blurb: Rendered civic modernism in crisp geometry, stone and glass, most iconically the Louvre's steel-and-glass pyramid.
works: East Building, National Gallery of Art

name: Ma Yansong
blurb: Leads MAD Architects toward sinuous, organic 'Shanshui' forms that blur buildings into landscape and futurist emotion.

name: Wang Shu
blurb: Builds from salvaged bricks and tiles, weaving vernacular craft and memory into contemporary Chinese architecture.
works: China Academy of Art, Xiangshan Campus

name: Arne Jacobsen
blurb: Danish functionalist who unified building and furniture, from the SAS Royal Hotel to the Egg and Ant chairs.

name: Bjarke Ingels
blurb: Founder of BIG, known for playful "hedonistic sustainability" like the ski-slope-topped CopenHill power plant.

name: Henning Larsen
blurb: Danish master of daylight whose luminous stone and glass civic halls balance Nordic restraint with sculptural monumentality.

name: Jorn Utzon
blurb: Pritzker laureate whose sculptural, sail-roofed Sydney Opera House redefined twentieth-century architecture.

name: Hassan Fathy
blurb: Reviver of Nubian mudbrick who resurrected vaults, domes and passive cooling to build dignified, low-cost villages for Egypt's rural poor.
credit: Dimitri Papadimos personal archive with his son Ioannis D. Papadimos

name: Alvar Aalto
blurb: Softened modernism with organic curves, warm timber and undulating brick, pioneering bent-plywood furniture that made functionalism humane.

name: Eliel Saarinen
blurb: Finnish National Romantic whose granite railway halls and towers bridged Art Nouveau and the American skyscraper before he emigrated.

name: Auguste Perret
blurb: Pioneered reinforced-concrete architecture, turning a structural technique into a refined classical language that rebuilt Le Havre after the war.

name: Charlotte Perriand
blurb: Shaped modern living through tubular-steel furniture and mountain interiors, blending machine-age rationalism with warm natural materials and Japanese craft.

name: Claude Nicolas Ledoux
blurb: Visionary of French Neoclassicism whose utopian saltworks and geometric toll-gates pushed pure form toward a radical ideal architecture.

name: Dominique Perrault
blurb: Minimalist of monumental scale and metallic mesh, known for embedding vast civic buildings into landscape and ground.

name: Jean Nouvel
blurb: Pritzker laureate whose contextual, light-modulating buildings respond uniquely to place, from mashrabiya screens to a floating desert dome.

name: Le Corbusier
blurb: Pioneer of modern architecture and the International Style, championing raw concrete, pilotis and the house as a machine for living.

name: Odile Decq
blurb: Provocateur of sweeping red-hued, curvilinear interiors, fusing high-tech structure with a punk, feminist sensibility.

name: Erich Mendelsohn
blurb: Pioneered Expressionist modernism with sweeping streamlined forms, epitomised by the sculptural Einstein Tower and his dynamic department stores.

name: Frei Otto
blurb: Pioneer of lightweight tensile and membrane structures whose forms were derived from studying nature.

name: Gottfried Böhm
blurb: Sculpted raw concrete into soaring, crystalline sacred spaces, most famously the mountainous pilgrimage church at Neviges.

name: Karl Friedrich Schinkel
blurb: Shaped Prussian Neoclassicism across Berlin, giving the capital museums, churches and guardhouses of severe, luminous Greek-revival clarity.

name: Ludwig Mies van der Rohe
blurb: "Less is more" master of minimalist steel-and-glass modernism and the International Style.

name: Walter Gropius
blurb: Founder of the Bauhaus school, fusing art, craft and industry into functional modern design.

name: David Adjaye
blurb: Designer of the bronze-latticed Smithsonian African American museum, weaving material, filtered light and diaspora memory into monumental civic architecture.
works: Smithsonian National Museum of African American History and Culture

name: Dimitris Pikionis
blurb: Poet of place who paved the Acropolis approaches in hand-set stone, binding Greek tradition and terrain into walkable landscape.

name: Balkrishna Doshi
blurb: Pritzker laureate who fused modernism with Indian vernacular in humane low-cost housing, campuses and institutions.

name: Bijoy Jain
blurb: Founder of Studio Mumbai, crafting hand-built houses of stone, timber and water where artisan skill and site shape every joint.

name: Charles Correa
blurb: Pioneered climate-responsive modernism with open-to-sky spaces, courtyards and low-cost urban housing rooted in Indian traditions.

name: Hafeez Contractor
blurb: Prolific shaper of India's post-liberalization skyline, delivering supertall luxury towers, stadiums and township-scale campuses across booming Mumbai and beyond.

name: Raj Rewal
blurb: Known for monumental modern buildings rooted in India's traditional urban forms, dense fabric and stone-lattice craft.

name: Rifat Chadirji
blurb: Father of modern Iraqi architecture who fused reinforced concrete with Abbasid arches and brickwork into a distinctive International Regionalism.

name: Grafton Architects (Farrell & McNamara)
blurb: Dublin practice crafting tactile, monumental civic and university buildings in concrete and stone, honoured with the 2020 Pritzker Prize.

name: Aldo Rossi
blurb: Theorist of Neo-Rationalism who revived archetypal urban forms and collective memory in built architecture.

name: Andrea Palladio
blurb: Renaissance master who distilled Roman order into serene symmetrical villas and temple-fronted facades that shaped classical architecture for centuries.

name: Carlo Scarpa
blurb: Craftsman-architect celebrated for meticulous detailing and the dialogue between modern intervention and historic fabric.

name: Filippo Brunelleschi
blurb: Founding father of Renaissance architecture who rediscovered linear perspective and raised Florence Cathedral's vast double-shell dome without centering.
credit: Nicolas de Larmessin and Esme de Boulonais

name: Gio Ponti
blurb: Restless polymath of Italian modernism whose slender crystalline towers and elegant furniture defined mid-century Milanese taste.

name: Massimiliano Fuksas
blurb: Sculptor of sweeping glass-and-steel gestures whose fluid canopies and cloud-like waves turn transport hubs into dramatic public spectacle.

name: Pier Luigi Nervi
blurb: Structural engineer-architect renowned for expressive reinforced-concrete vaults and elegant ferrocement stadiums and halls.

name: Renzo Piano
blurb: High-tech pioneer marrying lightweight engineering with generous daylight across cultural landmarks worldwide.

name: Arata Isozaki
blurb: Restless shape-shifter who moved from brutalist concrete to playful postmodern geometry, bridging Japanese tradition with global metropolitan ambition.
works: Museum of Contemporary Art, Los Angeles

name: Fumihiko Maki
blurb: Metabolist thinker of refined 'group form,' assembling elegant modular complexes in polished metal and layered urban fabric.

name: Kazuyo Sejima
blurb: Co-founder of SANAA, crafting weightless, transparent spaces of thin planes, glass and quiet minimalist clarity.
works: 21st Century Museum of Contemporary Art, Kanazawa
Glass Pavilion, Toledo Museum of Art

name: Kengo Kuma
blurb: Champions warm natural materials and layered timber lattices to soften modern buildings and reconnect them with place.
credit: Strelka Institute for Media, Architecture and Design

name: Kenzo Tange
blurb: Pioneered Japan's postwar Metabolism movement, fusing monumental modernist concrete with traditional Japanese proportion and civic scale.

name: Riken Yamamoto
blurb: Designs transparent, community-minded housing and civic buildings that dissolve barriers between private homes and shared public life.

name: Shigeru Ban
blurb: Turns humble paper tubes and cardboard into elegant structures, pioneering low-cost disaster-relief shelters alongside refined cultural landmarks.

name: Sou Fujimoto
blurb: Blurs the line between nature and building with airy, lattice-like structures that feel like inhabitable forests and clouds.

name: Tadao Ando
blurb: Self-taught master of smooth board-formed concrete, geometric purity and choreographed natural light framing silence and spirituality.

name: Toyo Ito
blurb: Conjures fluid, lightweight structures that dissolve boundaries, treating architecture as ephemeral flows of light, air and information.

name: Ken Yeang
blurb: Green-skyscraper pioneer whose bioclimatic towers use sky gardens, natural ventilation and ecology to make tall buildings breathe.

name: Luis Barragán
blurb: Master of emotional minimalism, composing vibrant colour planes, water and light within serene walled spaces.

name: Ricardo Legorreta
blurb: Carried Barragán's bold colour and monumental walls into large hotels, museums and civic landmarks.

name: Tatiana Bilbao
blurb: Socially engaged designer known for collage-driven forms and low-cost, adaptable sustainable housing.

name: Hendrik Petrus Berlage
blurb: Father of modern Dutch architecture, bridging honest brick craftsmanship and rational, stripped-down modernism.
credit: Amsterdam Municipal Department for the Preservation and Restoration of Historic Buildings and Sites (bMA)

name: Rem Koolhaas
blurb: OMA founder and theorist whose provocative, programme-driven buildings reshaped contemporary architectural thinking.
credit: Strelka Institute for Media, Architecture and Design

name: Winy Maas
blurb: MVRDV co-founder known for bold, data-driven buildings that stack, hollow and reinvent the urban block.

name: Kunlé Adeyemi
blurb: Creator of the triangular Makoko Floating School, prototyping buoyant, adaptable timber structures for African waterfront communities facing rising seas.

name: Kjetil Traedal Thorsen
blurb: Snohetta co-founder behind sweeping public landscapes you can walk upon, from Oslo's marble opera roof to Alexandria's tilted library.

name: Sverre Fehn
blurb: Norwegian who married Nordic modernism to site and landscape, threading concrete, timber and light through ruins and raw terrain.

name: Arif Hasan
blurb: Architect-activist behind Karachi's Orangi Pilot Project, championing community-built sanitation and incremental low-income housing over top-down urban planning.
works: Khuda Ki Basti incremental housing scheme

name: Habib Fida Ali
blurb: Restrained Pakistani modernist whose crisp corporate and campus buildings paired clean geometry with fine detail and quiet material discipline.
works: Indus Valley School of Art and Architecture
workname: Indus Valley School of Art and Architecture

name: Kamil Khan Mumtaz
blurb: Leading traditionalist reviving indigenous brick, lime and craft to give modern Pakistani buildings a cultural spirit of place.

name: Nayyar Ali Dada
blurb: Brick modernist whose Alhamra Arts Council became a defining landmark of contemporary Lahore architecture.

name: Yasmeen Lari
blurb: Pakistan's first female architect, who turned from brutalist towers to zero-carbon humanitarian bamboo-and-lime architecture.

name: Eduardo Souto de Moura
blurb: Known for stark granite and concrete works of quiet monumentality rooted in the Portuguese landscape.

name: Fernando Távora
blurb: Father of the Porto School who wove Portuguese vernacular craft and site with modern rigour into gently rooted buildings.
workcredit: Vitor Oliveira from Torres Vedras, PORTUGAL

name: Álvaro Siza
blurb: Master of restrained poetic modernism, sculpting light and white geometry precisely to landscape and site.

name: Antoni Gaudí
blurb: Pioneer of Catalan Modernisme whose organic, nature-inspired forms and mosaic surfaces defined Barcelona's cityscape.

name: Enric Miralles
blurb: Catalan visionary of restless fractured geometries whose layered, hand-drawn landscapes fused buildings into their terrain before his early death.

name: RCR Arquitectes
blurb: Pritzker-winning Catalan trio whose weathered-steel pavilions dissolve into landscape, framing light, water and shadow with poetic restraint.
credit: Maritza Ríos / Secretaría de Cultura CDMX

name: Rafael Moneo
blurb: Contextual rationalist whose museums and civic buildings weave modern order with the historical memory of place.
works: Cathedral of Our Lady of the Angels

name: Ricardo Bofill
blurb: Led Taller de Arquitectura, famed for monumental postmodern housing and the poetic reuse of industrial ruins.

name: Santiago Calatrava
blurb: Engineer-architect known for sculptural white skeletal structures inspired by the human body and natural forms.

name: Geoffrey Bawa
blurb: Father of tropical modernism, weaving open courtyards, water and lush landscape into buildings that breathe with Sri Lanka's climate.

name: Minnette de Silva
blurb: Trailblazing pioneer of modern regionalism who fused Corbusier's ideas with Sri Lankan crafts, courtyards and vernacular building traditions.

name: Gunnar Asplund
blurb: Swedish master who fused stripped classicism with modernism, shaping the serene, landscape-woven spaces of Stockholm's Woodland Cemetery.

name: Sigurd Lewerentz
blurb: Uncompromising Swede whose late brick churches, laid without cut bricks, turned raw material and dim light into sacred atmosphere.

name: Bernard Tschumi
blurb: Deconstructivist theorist who scattered bright red follies across Paris, arguing architecture is defined by events and movement, not form.

name: Herzog & de Meuron
blurb: Basel duo turning simple volumes into extraordinary surfaces, from a converted power station to a woven steel stadium.

name: Mario Botta
blurb: Ticinese master of geometric, symmetrical volumes in striped brick and stone, spanning banks, houses, churches and museums.
works: Santa Maria degli Angeli chapel, Monte Tamaro
Church of San Giovanni Battista, Mogno

name: Peter Zumthor
blurb: Pritzker laureate of atmosphere and materiality, crafting slow, sensory buildings rooted in site, texture and light.

name: Duangrit Bunnag
blurb: Reinvents warehouses and resorts with raw, tropical modernism, turning riverside industry into vibrant creative and communal destinations.

name: Mimar Sinan
blurb: Chief Ottoman court architect who perfected the domed mosque, crowning classical Ottoman architecture with the Selimiye.

name: Christopher Wren
blurb: Defined English Baroque, rebuilding fifty City churches after the Great Fire and crowning London with the vast dome of St Paul's.

name: David Chipperfield
blurb: Restrained modernist celebrated for material precision and the sensitive restoration of damaged historic buildings.

name: Edwin Lutyens
blurb: Master of the Edwardian country house who fused classical grandeur with English craft, from Castle Drogo to New Delhi's imperial capital.

name: Norman Foster
blurb: High-tech pioneer known for sleek steel-and-glass towers and structurally expressive, energy-conscious engineering.

name: Richard Rogers
blurb: Co-founder of high-tech architecture, famed for pushing structure and services to a building's colourful exterior.

name: Thomas Heatherwick
blurb: Blends sculpture, engineering and craft into experiential landmarks, from the Seed Cathedral to New York's climbable Vessel and Little Island.
credit: Strelka Institute for Media, Architecture and Design

name: Zaha Hadid
blurb: Pioneer of neo-futurist parametric design defined by sweeping curves and fluid, seemingly gravity-defying forms.

name: Daniel Libeskind
blurb: Creates jagged, deconstructivist forms charged with memory and emotion, from the zinc-clad Jewish Museum Berlin to Ground Zero's master plan.

name: Eero Saarinen
blurb: Sculpted mid-century modernism into soaring, expressive curves, turning airports and monuments into swooping structural gestures of flight and motion.

name: Frank Lloyd Wright
blurb: Pioneer of organic architecture, weaving Prairie-style houses and flowing interiors into their natural landscapes.
credit: New York World-Telegram and the Sun staff photographer: Al Ravenna

name: Jeanne Gang
blurb: Shapes sculptural, ecologically driven towers like the rippling Aqua, using structure to connect people with nature and community.

name: Louis Kahn
blurb: Master of monumental modernism, shaping weighty masonry, pure geometry and choreographed natural light.

name: Louis Sullivan
blurb: Coined "form follows function" and shaped the first steel skyscrapers with ornamented, vertically expressed towers that defined the Chicago School.

name: Michael Graves
blurb: Led postmodernism with playful, colorful, historically referenced buildings and household objects that reintroduced ornament and wit to design.

name: Peter Eisenman
blurb: Pioneered a cerebral, deconstructivist architecture of fractured grids and theory-driven form that questioned meaning and structure itself.
works: Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe

name: Philip Johnson
blurb: Brought the glassy International Style to America, then pivoted to playful postmodernism.

name: Richard Meier
blurb: Builds luminous white, geometrically pure buildings flooded with natural light, extending the rationalist legacy of early European modernism.

name: Robert Venturi
blurb: Father of postmodernism who countered "less is more" with complexity, symbolism and everyday vernacular.
credit: todd sheridan from New York, United States

name: Steven Holl
blurb: Designs phenomenological architecture where light, water, and material craft spatial experience, from Helsinki's Kiasma to porous urban hybrids.
credit: Museum of Contemporary Art Kiasma, Finland

name: Vo Trong Nghia
blurb: Champions bamboo and greenery as structure, bringing trees, gardens and low-cost natural materials back into dense tropical cities.
